basic_information.name: Haystack (by deepset)
basic_information.creator: deepset GmbH (Berlin, Germany) — co-founded by Milos Rusic, Malte Pietsch, and Timo Moller in June 2018
basic_information.description: Haystack is an open-source Python AI orchestration framework for building customizable, production-ready LLM applications. It uses a modular, pipeline-based architecture (DAG-style) where components — models, vector DBs, file converters, retrievers, generators — connect into reusable pipelines. Originally launched in 2019 as an NLP/semantic search framework, it has evolved into a full RAG and agentic AI platform. Haystack is notable as the only major open-source RAG framework from an EU-based company, making it especially relevant for GDPR-conscious deployments. With 24k+ GitHub stars and backing from GV and Balderton Capital, it competes directly with LangChain and LlamaIndex while emphasizing production-readiness and enterprise support.
basic_information.release_date: Initial release: November 2019; Haystack 2.0 stable: early 2024; Latest version: 2.21.0 (January 7, 2026)

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Pipeline-based DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) orchestration framework with support for branching, looping, and agent workflows. Pipelines are serializable to YAML/Python, cloud-agnostic, and Kubernetes-ready. Components are modular and swappable — each represents a node in the pipeline graph. The architecture supports both synchronous pipelines and agentic workflows with tool-calling.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Framework-agnostic — supports any embedding dimension through integrations with all major embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face Sentence Transformers, Jina, Voyage AI, Google, etc.). No fixed dimension constraint.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: Not applicable directly — Haystack delegates indexing to integrated document stores/vector databases. Supports HNSW (via Qdrant, Weaviate, Chroma), IVF (via Milvus), DiskANN (via Qdrant), flat (via in-memory store), and database-native indexes (via Elasticsearch, pgvector, MongoDB Atlas). Haystack's own InMemoryDocumentStore uses BM25 for sparse and cosine/dot-product for dense retrieval.
technical_architecture.scalability: Designed for enterprise-scale deployments. Scales horizontally via Kubernetes. Supports multi-tenancy through metadata filtering. Pipeline serialization enables reproducible deployments across environments. Hayhooks provides REST API deployment for production scaling. Enterprise Platform supports VPC, on-premise, and air-gapped deployments.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Self-hosted (Docker, Kubernetes), cloud-managed via Haystack Enterprise Platform (SaaS), deepset Studio (free visual builder with hosted infrastructure), VPC deployment, on-premise, air-gapped environments. Hayhooks enables turning pipelines into REST APIs or MCP servers.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector retrieval, sparse BM25 retrieval, hybrid retrieval (combining dense + sparse), multi-query retrieval (QueryExpander + MultiQueryTextRetriever/MultiQueryEmbeddingRetriever for improved recall). Supports metadata filtering, top-k retrieval, and score-based thresholding. Compatible with all major vector databases for retrieval.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Fixed-size character-based chunking, sentence-boundary-based splitting (preserving natural text flow), and as of v2.20+ semantic chunking via EmbeddingBasedDocumentSplitter (splits based on semantic similarity rather than fixed sizes). Document-structure-aware processing through file converters (PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown). Recursive splitting available through custom components.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in reranking components including TransformersSimilarityRanker (cross-encoder models), NvidiaRanker (NVIDIA NeMo Retriever), CohereRanker, and JinaRanker. Reranking is especially valuable in hybrid retrieval pipelines where results come from different datastores. Supports score fusion and metadata-boosted ranking.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Full multimodal RAG pipeline support: ImageFileToDocument for image ingestion, DocumentTypeRouter for mime-type routing, DocumentToImageContent for converting images, LLMDocumentContentExtractor for extracting text from images. Can build vision+text RAG pipelines. Supports image processing, image generation (via DALL-E integration), and audio transcription. Multimodal Agent available via fastRAG integration.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: Supported via Neo4j integration (neo4j-haystack): stores documents as graph nodes with vector search index for dense retrieval. EntityExtractor component enables named entity extraction and structured data identification. Can enrich or create knowledge graphs from unstructured text. GraphRAG patterns documented in deepset blog. Not a first-class built-in feature but well-supported through the integration ecosystem.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Built-in citation and grounding capabilities: (1) FaithfulnessEvaluator — splits generated answers into statements and checks each against contexts using an LLM; (2) Reference Predictor — annotates responses with academic-style citations per statement; (3) Hallucination detector for RAG — determines if model output accurately reflects source documents. These components can be added to any RAG pipeline for production-grade source attribution.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Pipeline-based approach allows flexible context management: configurable top-k retrieval limits, document truncation components, metadata filtering to reduce irrelevant context, reranking to prioritize most relevant chunks before LLM input. Multi-query retrieval expands recall without increasing context by deduplicating results. Prompt templates allow precise context formatting. No built-in compression or summarization-before-retrieval, but these can be implemented as custom pipeline components.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Framework overhead latency of approximately 5.9ms per query (pipeline orchestration overhead only, excluding model inference and retrieval). This is competitive with LlamaIndex (~6ms) and significantly faster than LangChain (~10ms) and LangGraph (~14ms). Actual end-to-end latency depends on chosen LLM, embedding model, and vector database.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Depends on deployment configuration and backend services. Hayhooks enables concurrent API serving. Enterprise Platform supports scaling for high-throughput production workloads. No published framework-specific QPS benchmarks, as throughput is primarily bottlenecked by LLM API calls and vector DB performance.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: Token usage is the lowest among major frameworks at approximately 1,570 tokens per query (vs. LlamaIndex ~1,600, DSPy ~2,030, LangGraph ~2,030, LangChain ~2,400). Built-in evaluation components: FaithfulnessEvaluator, ContextRelevanceEvaluator, SASEvaluator (Semantic Answer Similarity). Supports RAG-specific metrics including faithfulness, context relevance, and answer relevance.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: In standardized agentic RAG benchmarks (100 queries x 100 runs, same components across frameworks): Haystack achieved ~5.9ms overhead latency and ~1,570 tokens per query, placing it among the most efficient frameworks. No MTEB or BEIR scores as Haystack is an orchestration framework, not an embedding model. Performance depends on underlying model and DB choices. [uncertain]

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Haystack IS a framework/orchestrator itself, so it does not integrate 'into' LangChain or LlamaIndex. It is an alternative to them. However, Haystack components can interoperate with LangChain via custom adapters. Haystack has its own extensive integration ecosystem with 100+ integrations maintained by deepset and the community.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-4o, o1, o3), Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), Cohere (Command), Mistral AI, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, Azure OpenAI, Hugging Face (local and API-based models), NVIDIA NIM, Ollama (local models), Together AI, AI21 Labs, Fireworks AI, and more. All LLM generators support a standard function-calling interface.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Full MCP support since October 2025. MCPTool component enables Haystack pipelines to act as MCP clients connecting to MCP servers. MCPToolset dynamically discovers tools from MCP-compliant servers. Hayhooks can expose Haystack pipelines as MCP servers. Supports both Streamable HTTP/SSE and stdio connections. Available as mcp-haystack PyPI package.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Notion (NotionExtractor), Apify (web crawling), Mastodon. Document stores: Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Weaviate, Pinecone, Qdrant, Chroma, Milvus, pgvector, MongoDB Atlas, AstraDB, Neo4j, MarqoDB, LanceDB, InMemoryDocumentStore. File converters: PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, CSV, JSON, images. Custom connectors can be built as pipeline components. Enterprise Platform adds additional data ingestion connectors.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Built-in OpenTelemetry support and Datadog integration out of the box. Langfuse integration via langfuse-haystack package (traces pipeline execution, API calls, prompts, context data). Traceloop integration available. Compatible with standard OpenTelemetry exporters for any OTel-compatible backend. Enterprise Platform includes built-in monitoring and logging.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Open-core model: (1) Haystack open-source framework — free under Apache 2.0; (2) deepset Studio — free visual builder with usage limits for prototyping; (3) Haystack Enterprise Starter — paid support/services for teams using open-source Haystack in production; (4) Haystack Enterprise Platform — full managed platform with custom pricing based on organization size. Pricing is structured around platform licensing, agent/application runtime, and expert services.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Haystack open-source: fully free, unlimited use. deepset Studio: free with essential infrastructure and tooling for building and testing AI prototypes (usage-limited). Haystack Enterprise Platform Trial: free trial version available.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Open-source Haystack itself is free at any scale — costs come from infrastructure (compute, vector DB, LLM API calls). Enterprise Platform pricing is custom-quoted based on organization size and deployment model (cloud, hybrid, on-premise). No published per-query or per-vector pricing. deepset reported $12.5M ARR as of June 2024, suggesting enterprise contracts in the mid-five to six-figure range. [uncertain]
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: For self-hosted open-source: infrastructure costs (compute for pipeline serving, vector DB hosting, LLM API costs) plus engineering time for setup and maintenance. Haystack's modular design reduces vendor lock-in, allowing cost optimization by swapping components. Enterprise Platform adds managed infrastructure, SSO, support SLAs, and monitoring, reducing ops burden. Total TCO heavily depends on LLM provider choice (OpenAI vs. self-hosted open-source models) and vector DB selection.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Third-largest open-source RAG/LLM framework by GitHub stars, behind LangChain (~100k+) and LlamaIndex (~40k+). Most mature enterprise ecosystem among the three, with established production deployments and the strongest European presence. Positioned as the production-grade, enterprise-focused alternative — strongest in regulated industries and European markets. Leader in search-heavy RAG applications.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Global 500 enterprises: Airbus, Intel, Netflix, Apple, Meta, Databricks, NVIDIA, PostHog, LEGO, Infineon, Alcatel-Lucent Enterprise, BetterUp, NOS Portugal, TELUS. Public sector: German Federal Ministry of Research (BMFTR), Baden-Wuerttemberg State, PD, Etalab (French government). Agriculture and insurance sector deployments documented.
adoption_and_market.community_size: GitHub: 24,137 stars, 2,592 forks, 103 open issues (Feb 2026). Discord: ~4,362 members. PyPI downloads: ~305,000/month (haystack-ai package). Active contributor community with GitHub Discussions. 83 employees at deepset (June 2024).
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total funding: $45.6M over 3 rounds. Seed: $1.6M (March 2021). Series A: $14M led by GV/Google Ventures (April 2022). Series B: $30M led by Balderton Capital with GV, System.One, Lunar Ventures, Harpoon Ventures (August 2023). Revenue: $12.5M ARR as of June 2024. Valuation not publicly disclosed.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: (1) LangChain — largest community, most integrations, best for rapid prototyping but API stability concerns; (2) LlamaIndex — best for data indexing/querying, fastest retrieval, MIT licensed; (3) DSPy — research-oriented, optimizes prompts programmatically; (4) Llama-Stack (Meta) — emerging competitor backed by Meta. Haystack differentiators: EU-based (GDPR advantage), strongest enterprise offering, most production-focused, visual builder (Studio), lowest token usage, built-in evaluation components, MCP server/client support.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Ideal for: (1) Startups building search-centric or document-heavy AI products (legal tech, insurance, healthcare, compliance) — Haystack's retrieval-first design shines here; (2) EU-based startups needing GDPR compliance — deepset is Berlin-based with EU data residency options; (3) Teams of 2-5 engineers who want production-ready pipelines without extensive custom infrastructure; (4) Budget: free for open-source, Studio free for prototyping, Enterprise for scaling (custom pricing); (5) Best fit when you need reliable, explainable RAG with citation/faithfulness tracking for regulated industries. Less ideal for: rapid prototyping of complex agent chains (LangChain may be faster), or pure data indexing tasks (LlamaIndex may be more focused).
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Build (self-hosted open-source): Best when you have Python engineering talent, need full customization, want to avoid vendor lock-in, or have strict data residency requirements. Studio (free managed): Best for prototyping and learning — validate your RAG approach before investing in infrastructure. Buy (Enterprise Platform): Best when you need SSO, SLAs, dedicated support, and managed infrastructure — reduces ops burden for teams without DevOps capacity. The progression path is natural: Studio -> Open-source self-hosted -> Enterprise Platform as you scale.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC in 1-2 days using Studio's visual builder and pre-built templates. Working RAG pipeline in code: 1-2 weeks for experienced Python developers using tutorials. Production deployment: 4-8 weeks including document processing pipelines, evaluation setup, and infrastructure hardening. Enterprise Platform can accelerate this with managed infrastructure and support. Hayhooks provides production REST API deployment with minimal additional code.
key_lessons: Start with Studio (free visual builder) to validate your RAG architecture before writing code — the drag-and-drop interface maps 1:1 to code, so nothing is wasted when you move to production.
Invest in evaluation from day one: Haystack's built-in FaithfulnessEvaluator and hallucination detector are critical for regulated use cases. Do not ship RAG without measuring faithfulness.
Use hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense vectors) with reranking as your default pattern — it consistently outperforms either method alone and Haystack makes this a few-line configuration change.

Haystack's EU origin is a genuine competitive advantage for European startups: GDPR compliance, EU data residency, and European investors (Balderton) signal long-term commitment to the European market.

The modular pipeline architecture means you can swap any component without rewriting your application — start with OpenAI embeddings for speed, then migrate to open-source models when unit economics demand it.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes — deepset Studio provides a free visual drag-and-drop pipeline builder with pre-built templates for common use cases (RAG, semantic search, agentic workflows). Pipelines can be tested in a built-in Playground, deployed with one click to hosted infrastructure, and exported as YAML or Python code. Available at studio.deepset.ai.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt engineering & no-code tools — Studio as visual RAG builder), Session 3 (AI project framing — Haystack pipelines as Build approach in Build vs Buy), Session 4 (Business models — deepset's open-core model as case study)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official deepset/Haystack documentation, GitHub API, Crunchbase, TechCrunch, Wikipedia, and peer-reviewed benchmark comparisons. GitHub stats verified directly via API on Feb 9, 2026.
confidence.cross_reference: GitHub stats confirmed via API. Funding confirmed across Crunchbase, TechCrunch, Balderton Capital announcement. Customer list confirmed on deepset.ai and Wikipedia. Benchmark data from LLM Practical Experience Hub standardized comparison (100 queries x 100 runs). PyPI download stats from pypistats.org.
confidence.caveats: Haystack 2.x was a major rewrite from 1.x (breaking changes, new API) — older tutorials and Stack Overflow answers for farm-haystack may not apply. Community and ecosystem are smaller than LangChain's. Enterprise pricing is opaque (custom-quoted). Revenue figure ($12.5M ARR) from GetLatka may not be independently verified. The 'MDX' language tag on GitHub is misleading — the codebase is Python but the repo contains documentation files. Graph RAG support is via integrations rather than built-in.
confidence.security_posture: Enterprise Platform: SSO with SAML, configurable data retention policies, data not used for model training. Deployment options include VPC, on-premise, and air-gapped environments for classified data. Dedicated security experts with SLA-backed response times. Open-source framework: standard Python security practices, no known specific RAG poisoning mitigations beyond retrieval filtering. No public SOC 2 certification mentioned. Pipeline serialization (YAML) requires trust in pipeline sources to avoid code injection.
